To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LC neurons exhibit phasic or "focused attention" and tonic or "behavioral flexibility" modes of activity, which are closely related to the performance of the animal in a visual attention task.

(i) LC neurons exhibit phasic or phasic-tonic modes of activity during performance of a visual discrimination task, (ii) the phasic mode is associated with good task performance and may promote focused or directed attention, whereas the phasic-tonic mode is associated with poor task performance and may reflect a state of high arousal or scanning attentiveness, and (iii) a model of electrotonic coupling of LC cells predicts the observed differences in LC activity and performance.

LC neurons exhibit phasic and tonic modes of activity that correspond to good and poor performance on a visual attention task, respectively, and that a computational model of these results suggests that alterations in electro-tonic coupling between LC neurons may produce the different activity patterns and corresponding differences in task performance.
